current_interpretation: Each FY2025 measurement is paired with exactly one applicable numeric limit. The draft joins each DMR measurement to a permit limit row by matching LIMIT_VALUE_ID and LIMIT_SET_SCHEDULE_ID from the measurement row, after filtering to monitoring periods that fall within Federal FY2025 (2024-10-01 through 2025-09-30). The measurement's own LIMIT_BEGIN_DATE and LIMIT_END_DATE are carried on the DMR row; period_in_limit_interval is computed but the measurement_limit_pair join keys on limit value and schedule identity rather than re-evaluating all overlapping limit intervals. On this fixture the join yields one pair per measurement and the unique_applicable_limit_per_measurement requirement is satisfied.
status: requirement authored; currently satisfied on this fixture
why_it_matters: Purpose A needs a single enforceable numeric limit per reported measurement before comparing reported values to limits. If multiple limits could govern the same measurement, exceedance determinations would depend on an unstated tie-break rule.
supporting_evidence_used: Structured fields named in ISSUES.md: permit_limits.csv LIMIT_BEGIN_DATE, LIMIT_END_DATE, LIMIT_VALUE_ID, LIMIT_SET_SCHEDULE_ID; dmr_measurements.csv MONITORING_PERIOD_END_DATE, PARAMETER_CODE, PERM_FEATURE_NMBR
evidence_snippets_used: 824 FY2025 measurement–limit pairs; uniqueness currently SATISFIED (no cardinality hole)
Join produced one pair per measurement
contracts_involved: unique_applicable_limit_per_measurement (UNIQUE, per measurement, candidates measurement_limit_pair, cardinality ONE)
alternatives_considered: Treat overlapping or staged limit interval rows as separate governing identities rather than collapsing to one limit per measurement
Treat catalog restatements of the same limit (duplicate LIMIT_VALUE_ID / schedule rows) as multiple applicable limits requiring explicit disambiguation
Re-match limits by permit, outfall, parameter, and monitoring-period intersection with limit begin/end dates instead of joining on the measurement row's embedded limit value and schedule keys
remaining_uncertainty: Whether overlapping or staged interval rows should remain separate identities rather than being forced to a single governing limit; whether catalog restatements of the same limit should count as multiples.
